questions.question:
D3 — Which review mode should govern this plan?
Project/branch/task: fixture repo on main; reviewing PLAN.md "Add saved project views" (per-member named filter+sort presets on a project task list).
ELI10: The mode sets my posture for the rest of the review. It decides whether I push you to build a bigger version, keep the plan exactly as written and stress-test it, or cut it to the smallest useful core. This is an enhancement to an existing task list (roughly 9–12 changed files, estimated), not a greenfield build or a bug fix. Nothing about the plan's approach changes by picking a mode; every scope change still gets its own yes/no question later.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too much expansion and a small feature grows a tail of half-wanted extras; too little and you ship personal-only views and re-discover the sharing and deleted-filter-reference problems in production.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because the plan is a solid enhancement, but the landscape check surfaced a few adjacent options (shared views, remember-last-state, canonical filter serialization) worth a neutral look before locking scope.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: how hard I push on scope, in either direction, before the 11-section deep review.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Current scope gets the full rigor pass; each adjacent idea is offered neutrally as add / defer / skip
✅ You choose per item; rejected ideas land in an explicit NOT-in-scope list
❌ More questions than HOLD SCOPE; a handful of extra decisions before the deep review

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description:
✅ I describe the 10x version and the platonic ideal, then recommend expansions enthusiastically
✅ Best if you want views to become a platform piece (shared, default, deep-linked) now
❌ Bigger diff, longer pilot, more surface to secure and test on a feature whose base pain is small

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description:
✅ Scope stays exactly as written; maximum rigor on failures, edge cases, error paths, tests
✅ Fastest path to a review report; no scope questions beyond defer/keep checks
❌ Sharing, remember-last-state, and filter-shape questions get noted, not offered as scope

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description:
✅ Strips to the minimum core (e.g. remember last filter state, or create+list only)
✅ Smallest diff, quickest pilot signal on whether members even want persistence
❌ Named views and update/delete may get cut; you re-plan them later if the pilot says yes

questions.question:
D4.1 — E1: Store views using the task list's existing filter/sort serialization?
Project/branch/task: main; saved project views plan, SCOPE EXPANSION, proposal 1 of 6.
ELI10: Your task list already turns filters and sort into some encoded shape (usually the URL query string). A saved view should persist exactly that shape, not a new hand-rolled JSON schema. Then saved views, URLs, and shared links all speak one language, and when you add a new filter next quarter, old views keep working without a migration.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Two filter encodings drift apart; every new filter needs a stored-view migration; deep links (E2) and shared views (E3) need translation code.
Recommendation: Add because it is the cheapest item here (human ~0.5 d / CC ~15 min) and it is the foundation E2–E4 stand on.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=5/10, C=3/10, D=n/a
Net: one canonical filter language now vs. a second schema you maintain forever.

options.label: Add to scope (recommended)
options.description:
✅ One filter encoding shared by URL, saved views, and future shared links; new filters need no view migration
✅ Round-trip test (encode → save → load → decode) becomes the single test that proves views work
❌ Requires locating and possibly tidying the existing serializer before the table schema is final

options.label: Defer to TODOS.md
options.description:
✅ Base plan proceeds with whatever column shape is fastest today
✅ Decision recorded so a later pass can converge the encodings
❌ Stored views written in the interim need a migration when you converge later

options.label: Skip
options.description:
✅ No constraint on the saved_views column design
✅ Zero coupling to the task list's URL handling
❌ Two filter schemas from day one; E2/E3 become translation projects instead of near-free

options.label: Hold (stop chain, discuss)
options.description:
✅ Pauses the expansion questions so we can talk this one through first
✅ Nothing is decided until you say so
❌ Delays the remaining five proposals and the deep review

questions.question:
D2 — Which review mode should govern this plan? (ledger row R1)
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-w6cXCj on main, PLAN.md: saved project views.
ELI10: The mode sets my posture for the rest of the review. Expansion means I pitch bigger versions and ask you about each. Selective means I keep your scope, harden it, and offer each add-on (like shared views, stale-filter handling) as a separate yes/no. Hold means no additions, maximum rigor on what is written. Reduction means I propose cuts to reach a minimum core.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too expansive and a two-week pilot balloons into a platform project; too tight and the schema gets locked into private-only views that are painful to open up later.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because this is an enhancement (est. 8-12 files) with two cheap structural hedges worth an explicit yes/no, and the pilot argues against a cathedral.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: how much I am allowed to tempt you versus how tightly I guard the pilot scope.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Current scope gets bulletproofed first: access rules, error paths, tests, observability. ✅ Each add-on (shared views, stale-filter handling, default view) is offered separately; you accept, defer, or skip. ❌ More questions than HOLD; a few extra decisions before the deep review starts.

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description: ✅ I describe the 10x version: shared and default views, view analytics, URL-shareable state. ✅ Best if saved views are the seed of a larger task-list platform. ❌ Pulls hard against a two-week pilot; risks building features the pilot cannot measure.

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description: ✅ Exactly the four bullets in PLAN.md, traced for every failure and edge case. ✅ Fastest path to a reviewed, shippable pilot. ❌ The visibility-column hedge and stale-filter handling are only raised as concerns, not offered as scope; private-only schema may need a migration later.

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description: ✅ Strips to the minimum: maybe save + reopen only, no update or picker polish. ✅ Lowest cost to learn whether anyone reuses views. ❌ Plan is already small; cuts here would mostly remove the update/delete endpoints that users expect on any saved object.

questions.question:
D3.0 — Seven expansion proposals are on the table. How should I walk them?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-w6cXCj on main, saved project views, SCOPE EXPANSION mode.
ELI10: The proposals are E1 project-shared views, E2 default views, E3 stale-filter handling, E4 URL-addressable views, E5 pilot instrumentation, E6 dirty-state Update/Save-as-new, E7 delight pack (rename, duplicate, save nudge, shortcut, empty state, page title). Each is a separate scope call. I can ask one question per item (7 questions, each Add / Defer / Skip / Hold), or first propose a smaller set, or batch them into groups. Dependencies: E2's project default needs E1; E4 cross-member links need E1; E5 is what makes the pilot metric real for everything else.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Per-item gives you full control at the cost of 7 prompts; batching is faster but risks lumping unrelated decisions together.
Recommendation: A because every proposal is independently shippable and this mode exists to let you weigh each one.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: decision precision versus prompt count.

options.label: Full per-item split (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Seven D3.k questions, one per proposal, each with Add / Defer / Skip / Hold, then a D3.final to confirm the set. ✅ No proposal is dropped or merged without your say. ❌ Seven prompts before the deep review begins.

options.label: Narrow first
options.description: ✅ I propose a smaller candidate set (my pick: E1, E3, E5) and you confirm the cut before per-item questions. ✅ Fewer prompts if you agree with the narrowing. ❌ You see my shortlist before the full menu; less aligned with expansion posture.

options.label: Batch into two groups
options.description: ✅ Two multi-select questions: structural (E1-E4) and polish/observability (E5-E7). ✅ Fast: two prompts. ❌ Multi-select flattens Add vs Defer into yes/no; deferrals need a follow-up.

questions.question:
D3.1 — E1: Project-shared views (ledger row S1)
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-w6cXCj on main, saved project views.
ELI10: Today the plan saves a view for one member only. E1 adds a `visibility` column (private or project) and a share toggle, so a teammate's saved view shows up in my picker. Fixes the stated pain once per team instead of once per member. Owner keeps edit/delete; others can open and duplicate. Even if you defer the sharing UI, adding the column now (private default) avoids an ownership migration later. Effort: human ~2 days / CC ~30 min. Risk: medium, it is a new permission surface that must reuse the existing project-membership check. E2's project default and E4's cross-member links depend on it.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Skip it and the schema locks in private-only; add it and the plan gains a permissions test matrix.
Recommendation: Add because the goal sentence is about the team, and the structural cost is one column plus one authorization branch.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: team-wide fix now versus a smaller permission surface for the pilot.

options.label: Add to scope (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Teammates reuse each other's views; the pain is fixed once per project. ✅ Column + owner-only mutation rule land together with their permission tests. ❌ Adds a permission matrix (owner, member, non-member) to test and a share toggle to design.

options.label: Defer to TODOS.md
options.description: ✅ Pilot stays private-only and smaller. ✅ Deferral recorded with context so the follow-up starts warm. ❌ Without the column now, sharing later means a data migration; I will ask separately whether to add the column alone.

options.label: Skip entirely
options.description: ✅ Smallest possible schema and permission surface. ✅ Nothing to design beyond the original four bullets. ❌ Orphans E2 project default and E4 cross-member links; goes to NOT in scope.

options.label: Hold, discuss first
options.description: ✅ Stops the chain so we can talk through the permission model before deciding. ✅ No disposition recorded until you say continue. ❌ Delays the remaining six proposals.
